checkpoints: Verify multiple edits within one burst reset the 120 ms timer and produce one write containing only the latest text.
Verify a later burst schedules and saves independently after the first burst has completed.
Verify empty-string edits are saved after the quiet interval.
Verify editing with no current Badge remains a no-op.
Verify pending edits remain associated with the document that was current when edit(text) accepted them, including across open, close, and dispose.
Verify departing pending edits are made persistent before a destination document is read, while synchronous navigation triggered by that save remains authoritative.
Verify current-document status filtering and subscription removal still work.
Verify Preview retains its 40 ms delay and hide() cancellation behavior.
Compile public Java sources with OpenJDK 11, placing generated classes outside /workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not write each accepted editor keystroke immediately to the store.
Do not redirect pending text to whichever document is current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or discard accepted document edits merely because the current Badge is detached, closed, replaced, or disposed.
Do not allow an outer open or close operation to overwrite document state installed by synchronous nested navigation during a save.
Do not change createWorkspace-equivalent public operations, source identity, text, status payload, or store revision semantics.
Do not change search-preview timing, coalescing, cancellation, or public behavior.
Do not make Badge own or destroy the persistent per-document buffer.
lifecycle_identity: Each document ID has one reusable Trailing buffer in Workspace's BufferBank.
Badge represents only the current view's document identity, buffer reference, and live store subscription.
An edit is bound at acceptance time to the buffer referenced by the current Badge.
Workspace generation identifies the currently authoritative open/close request; a request superseded by synchronous navigation must not install or clear a view afterward.
Detaching a Badge ends its subscription lifetime but does not end the lifetime of its document buffer or accepted pending text.

obligations.text: Workspace.edit(text) must capture the current Badge and push text into that Badge's reusable per-document Trailing buffer; when no Badge is current, it must do nothing.
The editor buffer must use a 120 ms trailing quiet interval: each new edit in a burst replaces the pending text and resets the timer, and expiry writes only the latest text for the captured document.
After a buffer flushes, its pending state and timer handle must already be retired so later bursts can save and synchronous reentrant activity cannot consume the same pending value twice.

Pending editor text must survive Badge retirement. To preserve persistence and destination reads across open, close, and dispose, retirement must detach and clear the departing presentation before flushing that departing Badge's pending buffer.

Because flushing can synchronously invoke store listeners that navigate, open must revalidate its captured generation after retirement before installing the requested Badge and emitting its document payload. Close must perform no stale visible effect after a nested navigation becomes authoritative.
BufferBank must continue to reuse an independent Trailing instance per document ID, and each buffer's consumer must preserve that ID when calling Environment.write(id,text).

Store writes must continue updating the record, incrementing revision, and synchronously notifying subscribed listeners; Badge must continue emitting status only for its own document ID and detach its captured subscription on retirement.
Preview is outside the maintenance change and must retain its separate 40 ms Trailing task, query push behavior, and hide cancellation.
Public interfaces and existing document/status payload shapes must remain unchanged.

ordering_barriers: On edit acceptance, resolve current Badge and its buffer before scheduling delayed work; do not resolve the document at timer execution time.
Trailing.push must cancel the prior handle before storing the latest pending text and scheduling the replacement 120 ms callback.
Trailing.flush must snapshot pending text and clear handle/pending state before invoking the callback-capable write consumer.

During retirement, revoke current ownership, detach the captured Badge subscription, and emit document clearing before flushing its buffer; otherwise navigation caused by the flush could be erased by stale outer cleanup.
During open, capture a new generation before retirement and compare it again after retirement, because retirement may flush and synchronously trigger nested navigation.
Install a destination Badge and read/output its document only if the open request still owns the generation.
preservation: Preserve Workspace open, edit, close, and dispose interfaces and Preview query and hide interfaces.
Preserve independent persistent document buffers owned by BufferBank and live subscriptions owned by Badge.
Preserve original document association for delayed text.
Preserve Store record, event id, text, revision increment, listener snapshot iteration, and synchronous notification behavior.
Preserve status filtering to the current Badge's ID and subscription cleanup on retirement.
Preserve document output payload fields id and text and the empty-string default returned by Store.read.
Preserve navigation authority when a save callback synchronously opens or closes the workspace.
Preserve Preview's existing separate 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancellation.
scope: Business behavior in src/Workflow.java concerning Workspace editor autosave, Trailing editor buffers, BufferBank reuse, Badge retirement, and navigation-safe persistence.
Read-only consideration of Store behavior needed to preserve editor semantics.
Preview behavior is preservation-only and must not be modified for this maintenance task.

Railway operations — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: separate BufferBank service

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.
void push(String text) { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); pending=text; handle=env.schedule(this::flush,delay); }
void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }

static final class Badge {final String id;final Trailing buffer;final Environment env;final int token;Badge(Environment env,String id,Trailing buffer){this.env=env;this.id=id;this.buffer=buffer;token=env.store().subscribe(e->{if(id.equals(e.get("id")))env.output("status",e);});}void detach(){env.store().stop(token);}}

static final class BufferBank {final Map<String,Trailing> entries=new HashMap<>();Trailing get(Environment env,String id){return entries.computeIfAbsent(id,k->new Trailing(env,120,text->env.write(k,text)));}}
